$note: Settings that GitHub holds and no file in the repository can make it read. `node .github/scripts/repo-settings.mjs` reads every part back and exits 0 only when each equals this data; `--apply` writes the rulesets and the environment from it (never the deploy key, never a secret: the owner makes those by hand, see README). A change of this file needs the owner's word.

environment.$note: The owner alone reviews: prevent_self_review is false so that the owner can dispatch and approve the same run. can_admins_bypass is sent on apply and compared only when the API shows it; if it does not, the owner sets it by hand (Settings > Environments > release > unticks 'Allow administrators to bypass configured protection rules') and the record says so with the date. The secret is named here and set by the owner; it must exist in this environment only, never as a repository secret.
environment.name: release

deployKey.$note: One key, titled release-promotion, writable. `key` is the public line the owner's ssh-keygen printed (step 3 of the apply order); until a pull request writes it here the read-back reports it as missing.
deployKey.title: release-promotion

actions.$note: Story 2.1 set these; this is their read-back.
